content: Streamlines recruiting and enrolling participants in clinical trials by orchestrating each stage from initial recruitment to enrollment. Provides a unified clinical trial portal experience for potential participants and coordinators. Benefits: reduce cost per eligible participant, reduce cost per consenting participant conversion, reduce average time between registration and enrollment, improve participant experience, lower attrition rate.

recruitment: Criteria-based search and filter for trial discovery on Experience Cloud sites
OmniStudio components for digitizing prescreening and registration
AI candidate matching to automatically match candidates to trials

data_model: FHIR R4 and USCDI-aligned for interoperability

content: During recruitment, potential participants are called Candidates. The recruitment phase supports: trial discovery via criteria-based search on self-service portals, candidate matching using AI to automatically match candidates to eligible trials, prescreening through digitized OmniStudio components, and the application process. Clinical trial managers create records for care programs (representing clinical trials) and research studies. Key records: care programs, research studies, enrollment criteria, site associations.
gotchas: Candidates become Participants only after enrollment is complete
AI matching requires configuration of matching criteria per trial
Self-service portal requires Experience Cloud setup

content: Manage complex therapies including cell and gene therapies with chain of custody tracking. Key features: custody item tracking, custody chain entries with signature trails, electronic signatures for chain of custody verification, care program enrollee management, and therapy scheduling. Each custody item can have multiple custody chain entries, and each entry has a signature trail that appears on the care program enrollee's record page when ready for signing.
gotchas: Chain of custody requires electronic signatures — cannot be skipped for regulatory compliance
Each custody chain entry requires its own signature trail
Advanced therapy management is a specialized add-on — separate from standard clinical engagement

description: Participant Management supports clinical trial participant tracking. The data model aligns with FHIR R4 resources and USCDI data classes for health data interoperability. Key objects include ClinicalTrialParticipant, ClinicalEncounter, and ClinicalObservation. USCDI alignment ensures that health data captured during clinical engagement can be shared with EHR systems. Person Account is the foundation - participants are Person Accounts with additional clinical attributes.
setup_steps: Set up FHIR R4 resource mapping for interoperability
gotchas: Person Account enablement is IRREVERSIBLE - once enabled, cannot be disabled
FHIR alignment is data model alignment, not a built-in FHIR API endpoint
USCDI compliance requires explicit field mapping between platform objects and USCDI data classes
migration_relevance: Clinical engagement is largely net-new capability. No direct Veeva equivalent for most clinical objects.

description: Advanced Therapy Management supports complex therapies (cell and gene therapy, specialty infusions, rare disease treatments) that require coordinated multi-step workflows. Therapy scheduling, preparation tracking, administration logging, and follow-up monitoring are managed as a connected workflow. Chain of custody tracking ensures product integrity from manufacturing through administration. Cold chain management tracks temperature compliance.
setup_steps: Configure therapy types and workflow templates
Set up chain of custody tracking points
Set up therapy scheduling with resource allocation
gotchas: Chain of custody gaps are compliance violations - tracking must be continuous
Cold chain temperature excursions must trigger immediate alerts
Multi-step therapy workflows require strict sequencing enforcement
migration_relevance: Specialized capability for cell and gene therapy. Typically net-new for most migrations.
